rv.q: Neilson’s expertly acted production is one long sleight of hand.
It's weird, nauseating and extremely fun.
It's a deft, macabre turn by Neilson, who also directs.
Yet while there's plenty of twisted humour, it feels like a cheeky sketch that's been extended beyond its ideal length.
It’s hard to see how this dramatic mutant will win an audience.

cn.t: Neilson's grotesque, darkly comic riff on Poe divides critics with its visceral gore and surreal Christmas staging. Most praise its bracingly disruptive imagery, though some find the over-extended plot undermines the horror.
